title: Check what a cut takes away
statement: Before cutting or trimming part of a lesson, check what only it supplies and what later lessons ask of it.
example: One audit found a later unit's two transfer questions pointing at exactly the two ideas the served lessons failed to land.
detail: A curriculum adherence audit (`grade3-reading/artifacts/curriculum-adherence-2026-09-24/REPORT.md`, 2026-09-24) compared four served lessons with their designs and with a later unit's transfer questions. One lesson had halved its key idea, that a setting sets the rules and the mood, to mood alone, while the later unit asks where else the child has seen a setting set the rules and the mood; two of that unit's transfer questions point at exactly the two ideas two of the lessons fail to land. The same audit found that cutting an added word routine the design forbids would leave the child with no old-London background at all, because the film meant to carry it did not and the knowledge page designed for it was absent. A halved idea leaves a later question pointing at something the learner never met.

evidence.quote: L4 threshold halved to mood; the rules half weakened (core; L4).
Cross-course dependency: WITW L11 Use it (PR #613) asks "Where else have you seen a setting set the rules and the mood? Think about Peter Pan."
WITW L11/L14 Form B now point at exactly the two ideas L4 and L7 fail to land
Picking our four Name-it sentences without those two ideas leaves WITW pointing at content the child never met
the child would meet no old-London context at all
